findings.evidence: 'When the user asks for proposed commands, label them as proposed and do not claim they ran' and step 2's 'Plan each commit as paths, plus hunks for a mixed file' primarily restate ordinary request-following and commit planning the model already knows, unlike the surrounding temporary-index and hook safeguards.
findings.fix: Fold proposal labelling into the existing routing table and combine path/hunk planning with the staging decision. Remove the standalone generic reminders while retaining the non-obvious index, verification and hook procedures.

findings.evidence: 'Repeat steps 3-7' repeats step 3's instruction to create a new mktemp run directory, but 'Afterwards remove <run>' only cleans up the latest directory. Following a two-commit plan literally leaves the first directory's index, patches and verification export behind without the required leftover report.
findings.fix: Allocate one run directory before the per-commit loop and reuse it, recreating its verification export for each commit. Alternatively, clean up each owned run directory before allocating the next. Preserve cleanup or an explicit leftover report on every exit.

findings.evidence: 'Afterwards ... in temporary-index mode, run git reset -q -- <committed paths>' delays real-index synchronization until the entire commit sequence finishes. When two approved changes to the same path are split across successive temporary-index commits, the first commit leaves that path appearing as a staged reversal in the real index. The next step-3 overlap check sees an unapproved staged diff and stops the otherwise approved second commit.
findings.fix: After each successful, tree-matched temporary-index commit, synchronize only that commit's approved paths in the real index before starting the next planned commit. First enforce the overlap safeguard against unapproved pre-existing staged content, and leave all other index entries unchanged.
